$comment: §4.1c mutation coverage. Each entry is a CONCRETE PATCH: a file, a find
string that must occur exactly once, and its replacement, plus the rendered
verdict/measurement marker it kills, the test that kills it, and the shared
helper that test must run. A kill counts only when the unmutated baseline
passed in the same run, the patch changed the file, the run served the
MUTATED bundle (its hash moved), and the failure is the owning test's own.
mutations/run.mjs enforces all four; e2e/global-teardown.ts additionally
fails the run if a recorded kill's (test, marker) assertion never executed,
judged at RUNTIME from e2e/observations.ts, not from spec source.

mutations.test: mitm recovers x exactly at the published size
mutations.why: Removes the ⊕ δ tamper. With no perturbation every session behaves honestly, every bit reads 0, and the recovered x no longer matches the real key.

mutations.test: a noiseless session at t = 0 is ACCEPTED
mutations.why: Changes the reader's accept rule from ≤ t to < t. A noiseless honest session at t = 0 has zero failures: ≤ accepts, < rejects.

mutations.test: the observed false-reject frequency is substantial at the published threshold
mutations.why: Forces the tag's noise bit to 0. Honest sessions then never fail a check, so the observed false-reject frequency collapses from ~0.44 to 0.

mutations.test: the false tag recovers y exactly once x is known
mutations.why: Adds noise to the false tag's reply (flips it). The reader's failures no longer track b·y, so the recovered y is wrong.

mutations.test: mitm recovers x exactly at the published size
mutations.why: Replaces 'any acceptance means the bit is 0' with a majority vote over m sessions. A zero bit accepts only ~56% of the time, so a majority of m misreads it ~28% of the time and the recovered x is wrong.

mutations.test: the exact false-reject rate is 0.4403 at r = 80, t = 20
mutations.why: Starts the false-reject sum at i = t instead of t + 1, adding the i = t term. P_FR is no longer 0.4403.

mutations.test: the chosen-challenge attack recovers and verifies x
mutations.why: Skips the pivot row swap in Gaussian elimination. The default random challenge set needs several swaps, so the elimination produces a wrong x and the verification run rejects it.

mutations.find: const expected = (dot(a, this.x) ^ dot(b, this.y)) as Bit;
mutations.replace: const expected = (dot(a, this.x) ^ (dot(b, this.y) & 0)) as Bit;
mutations.test: exhibit 1 Row 3 renders an HB+ check that passes
mutations.why: Drops the b·y term from the HB+ reader's check. On Row 3 (b·y = 1, ν = 0) the correct check passes but the mutated check fails.
